key_insight: The paper shows that humanoid loco-manipulation can be learned from synthetic vision-language-kinematics (VLK) data generated in reconstructed 3D scenes, bridging the gap between what the robot sees, what it is told, and how it should move. This creates scalable supervision for training whole-body agents without requiring scarce real-world synchronized demonstrations.
problem_solved: Existing datasets do not provide large-scale synchronized tuples of egocentric images, language instructions, and robot-compatible kinematic trajectories, making it difficult to train humanoids for perception-based loco-manipulation.
method: Reconstruct real scenes using 3D Gaussian Splatting to create interactive environments.
Generate synthetic VLK supervision by pairing egocentric visual observations with language commands and corresponding humanoid motion trajectories.
Train and evaluate humanoid loco-manipulation policies using this synthetic data pipeline to connect perception, instruction understanding, and whole-body control.
impact: This work offers a practical path to scale humanoid training data for complex embodied tasks, reducing dependence on expensive human teleoperation or real robot collection. For AI/ML practitioners, it suggests a reusable framework for building richer multimodal training corpora in simulation-like reconstructed worlds.
